query: Socioeconomic indicators, crowdsourced data, and non-traditional data sources as alternatives/complements to NFIP claims for measuring flood damage at ZCTA level
sub_questions: 311/non-emergency service request data as flood impact proxy
Property value changes (ZTRAX, CoreLogic) as post-flood damage signals
Social media and crowdsourced flood reports (Twitter, Waze, CoCoRaHS, USGS STN)
Infrastructure disruption data (EAGLE-I, 511 road closures, cellular, school closures)
Displacement and demographic signals (USPS NCOA, ACS, mobile phone data, shelter data)
Health and mortality signals (CDC WONDER, Medicare claims, EMS call data)
gaps: 311 under-reporting bias correction is nascent (single Bayesian model paper)
Waze flood validation rests on a single Nature Scientific Reports study
No national standardized 311 flood complaint category taxonomy exists
EAGLE-I is county-level only; ZIP-level power outage data requires commercial sources
Twitter/X API access effectively closed for academic research post-2023
EMS/911 call data not publicly archived at ZIP level
CDC WONDER mortality data suppressed at ZCTA level due to small counts
Mobile phone displacement data (SafeGraph, Cuebiq, Meta) requires data agreements
